natural_body: 40% discount lifts acquisition and revenue but cuts 30-day retention 12%; use selectively.

first.rationale: Activation and onboarding completion are both down 4-6% QoQ. memory_31 and memory_86 show that simplification durably lifts early adoption in self-serve cohorts. Verifying memory_31 (signup field reduction) and memory_91 (activation messaging lift) will validate whether we can compound these effects. This addresses both headline metrics without the retention risk of memory_73 (40% discount cuts 30-day retention 12%) or competitive trap of matching aggressive pricing. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is valuable but doesn't address the SMB activation decline. Referral incentive (memory_57) works in established base, not acquisition-stage friction. A standard experiment on simplified onboarding targets the root problem and plays to our documented strength.
